extensions.description: Operations for compiling, assembling, bundling, and distributing software artifacts.
extensions.example: STE: Build the Docker image. Then deploy the container to the registry. | Non-STE: Perform a build of the Docker image and then do a deployment to the registry.

extensions.description: Operations for verifying code correctness, measuring performance, and ensuring quality.
extensions.example: STE: Run the test suite. Check that the coverage is above 80 percent. | Non-STE: Execute the test suite and verify that coverage exceeds 80%.

extensions.description: Operations for installing, updating, locking, and resolving software dependencies.
extensions.example: STE: Install the dependencies with npm install. Pin the versions in the lock file. | Non-STE: Snag the deps and bump the versions.

extensions.description: Operations for tracking changes, branching, merging, and collaborating on source code.
extensions.example: STE: Commit the changes. Then push the branch to the remote repository. | Non-STE: Git the changes and then push them up. (Uses Git as a verb, Rule 1.7 violation)

extensions.description: Operations for authentication, authorization, encryption, and protecting systems from threats.
extensions.example: STE: WARNING: Sanitize all user input before you process it. Unsanitized input can cause SQL injection attacks. | Non-STE: CAUTION: Always clean your inputs.

extensions.description: Operations for recording events, measuring system health, and observing runtime behavior.
extensions.example: STE: Log the error details to the error file. Monitor the CPU usage. | Non-STE: Do a logging of the exception. Keep an eye on the CPU.

extensions.description: Concepts for designing, documenting, and consuming application programming interfaces.
extensions.example: STE: The endpoint returns a JSON object. The object contains a user list and a pagination token. | Non-STE: The API method gives you back a JSON with the users and a next-page thing.

extensions.description: Operations for setting up, managing, and maintaining system and application configuration.
extensions.example: STE: Set the DATABASE_URL environment variable in the .env file. | Non-STE: Tweak the DATABASE_URL knob in the dotenv thing.

extensions.description: Concepts and operations specific to object-oriented programming paradigms.
extensions.example: STE: The UserRepository class extends BaseRepository. It implements the IAuditable interface. Inject the Database dependency through the constructor. | Non-STE: The repo subclasses the base and hides the data. Pass the DB in via the ctor.

extensions.description: Concepts and operations specific to functional programming paradigms.
extensions.example: STE: Map the transformation over the list. Then fold the results with the sum function. | Non-STE: Loop over the array applying the transform and then add everything up.

extensions.description: Concepts and operations for memory management, ownership, lifetimes, and low-level system access.
unapproved_alternatives: shooting yourself in the foot → undefined behavior
extensions.example: STE: Allocate a buffer on the heap. Deallocate the buffer before the function returns. The borrow checker prevents dangling pointers. | Non-STE: Malloc a chunk of memory and free it when you are done. Rust's thingy stops you from shooting yourself in the foot.

extensions.description: Concepts for describing desired system state through configuration files and infrastructure-as-code.
extensions.example: STE: The Terraform resource provisions an AWS EC2 instance. Apply the configuration to converge the infrastructure. | Non-STE: Terraform spins up an EC2 box when you run the apply command.

extensions.description: Signal words and conventions for documenting security risks, breaking changes, and important notes in code.
extensions.example: STE: WARNING: DO NOT COMMIT THE API KEY. AN EXPOSED KEY CAN CAUSE UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS. | Non-STE: heads up: don't check in the secret key or bad things happen.

extensions.description: Standardized terms and formats for writing clear, consistent commit messages.
extensions.example: STE: feat: Add JWT authentication middleware for API routes. | Non-STE: Implemented JWT auth middleware for the API endpoints.

extensions.description: Operations and concepts for automated build, test, and deployment pipelines.
extensions.example: STE: The pipeline has three stages: build, test, and deploy. Trigger the workflow on every push to the main branch. | Non-STE: The CI kicks off when you push to main and runs the build, test, and deploy stuff.

extensions.description: Operations for querying, migrating, backing up, and managing database systems.
extensions.example: STE: Migrate the database schema to version 3. Seed the development database with test data. | Non-STE: Run the migration script to update the DB and populate it with fake data.

extensions.description: Terms for documenting UI components, interactions, and interface behavior.
extensions.example: STE: Click the Submit button. Type your password in the text field. | Non-STE: Hit the submit thing and enter your pwd in the box.
